name: Punugulu
ingredients: 2 cups dosa batter (fermented rice and urad dal batter)
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh coriander leaves
instructions: 1. In a large mixing bowl, take the fermented dosa batter and add chopped onions, green chilies, ginger, coriander leaves, cumin seeds, and salt.
2. Mix well to combine. If the batter is too thin, add a tablespoon of rice flour to achieve a thick dropping consistency.
3. Heat oil in a deep frying pan or kadhai over medium-high heat.
4. Carefully drop small portions of the batter into the hot oil using your fingers or a small spoon.
5. Fry the Punugulu in batches, turning them occasionally, until they turn golden brown and crisp on all sides.
6. Remove using a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels.
7. Serve hot with spicy peanut chutney or ginger chutney.
description: Punugulu is a quintessential Andhra street food, beloved for its crispy exterior and soft, airy interior. It is traditionally made using leftover fermented dosa batter, making it a popular household snack. It represents the resourceful and flavorful nature of Andhra cuisine and is a staple at local tiffin centers.
